newsitem.title: USA: Sierra Health falls on concerns over merger.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Health falls on concerns over merger.

text.p: Shares of Sierra Health Services Inc fell sharply on concerns its planned merger with Physician Corp of America might not yield the same cost savings as other mergers in the managed health care industry, analysts said.

"The trick in consolidating is to have geographic overlap," said Dave Shove, an analyst with Fox-Pitt, Kelton. "But when a company in Las Vegas buys a company in Florida or Texas, there is no consolidation and it hasn't made the system any more efficient."
The steep drop in its share price pushed the value of the merger down to about $434 million, from $509 million based on its closing price on Friday, before the acquisition was announced.

Sierra said it was looking for a merger that would make it a multi-state player, but analysts said that in pursuing such a strategy it missed out on one of the biggest benefits of consolidating: getting greater leverage from an existing provider network.
In addition, they noted that one of the regions Sierra chose as its route of expansion, Florida, is an especially tough market from a competitive and a regulatory standpoint.

The state's two big managed care companies, Humana Inc, and United Healthcare Corp have a relatively strong market position, and state regulators have allowed non-HMO plans to price below cost, they said.
